legal_reference: Geneva Conventions grave-breaches provisions; Rome Statute
conduct_examples: Wilful killing, torture, inhuman treatment, extensive destruction not justified by military necessity
analysis_note: Grave breaches trigger penal obligations under Geneva law.

conduct_examples: Intentionally directing attacks against civilian population or individual civilians not taking direct part
analysis_note: Requires distinction between civilians and lawful military objectives.

legal_reference: Additional Protocol I; Rome Statute; customary IHL
conduct_examples: Launching attack with excessive expected incidental civilian harm
analysis_note: Requires assessment of expected harm versus anticipated concrete and direct military advantage.

legal_reference: Additional Protocols; Rome Statute amendments; customary IHL
conduct_examples: Using starvation as method of warfare; unlawfully impeding humanitarian relief
analysis_note: Highly relevant in siege and humanitarian-access disputes.
